title: Only the Rich Are Poisoned: The Preferences of Others
coreMove: Interrogate whether a preference came from direct use or from status pressure imported into your life.
sourcePressure: Status and wealth can detach people from firsthand preference and make them vulnerable to desires manufactured by others.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating the chapter as envy of luxury or simple anti-consumerism.

sourceAnchors.name: Only the Rich Are Poisoned
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar supports wealth or status insulation as a distortion of direct preference and judgment.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The poison is not money itself; it is the moment someone else can sell you a desire you would never have formed from use.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: wine collector buying bottles praised by status circles but never enjoyed at dinner
exampleSpecs.audience: buyer separating taste from prestige contagion
exampleSpecs.stakes: money and identity follow a preference he did not form
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia opens one prized bottle with an ordinary meal and writes down whether she would buy it without the label.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cork split beside a plain plate

exampleSpecs.domain: executive choosing a private school because peers expect it
exampleSpecs.audience: parent testing borrowed preference against child fit
exampleSpecs.stakes: a child may carry the cost of status anxiety
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Vincent asks his daughter to rank the school day before he ranks the parent reception.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a glossy prospectus on a car seat

exampleSpecs.audience: reader seeing preference outsourced to taste authority
exampleSpecs.stakes: daily comfort could be traded for photographed approval
